summary: Read desired declarations, selected declaration tokens and cheap actual summaries together with fractal subject desired --json [--all | SUBJECT...] [--kind K]. The CLI follows bounded desired GET pages, collecting one final array without status reduction or cold card folds.

replay.detail: No graph replay or new authoritative projection. The desired(kind, subject) index is local query acceleration. A local desired-write generation is cursor invalidation state, advanced transactionally by triggers for every desired-row insert, update or delete, including replication repair.

schema.detail: Adds GET /v1/desired?subject=ID&subject=ID&kind=K&limit=N&cursor=TOKEN. Repeated URL-encoded subject names are optional (omission selects all); kind and cursor are optional. More than 1,000 supplied names returns desired-batch-limit. Page limit defaults to 1,000, with maximum 1,000; zero or over-limit values return HTTP 422 desired-page-limit. Each page is {items: DesiredBatchItem[], next_cursor: string|null, store_index: u64}. Items flatten DesiredSubject with nullable desired_token and optional extensible actual, including published mission definitions. A retained member with an unsupported enum variant anywhere in its schema, or an unknown field in a structure that rejects unknown fields, yields actual: {unavailable: {code: member-version-unproven}} only for that item; its member is omitted, its declaration and token remain, and other items retain normal actual summaries. The authority is the full MemberSpec serde schema, including nested discriminators and deny_unknown_fields structures, not a numeric wire version. Malformed JSON, wrong types, missing required fields and unrelated read failures still fail the page. The CLI preserves raw extensible item JSON, including newer member payloads and unavailable markers. This raw route is outside generated client-v0 schemas.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or declaration selection rule changes.

compatibility.detail: The desired collection GET inherits existing read.projections authorization, deadlines and read admission, including paired-device refusal without that scope, and works during fleet drain. Per-subject desired reads, subject cards, sparse summary and digest semantics are unchanged. Missing summary fields require fetching the card, not interpreting them as negative observations. A batch fails when a stored payload of a known member is malformed; unsupported newer member schemas instead retain the item with a member-version-unproven actual marker.

downtime.detail: Normal startup automatically creates the desired(kind, subject) query index on existing desired rows and installs the local desired-write witness and triggers before serving reads. This one-time index build adds startup work proportional to existing desired declarations; no offline migration or planned downtime is required.

manual.detail: No manual or offline installation step; ordinary store startup installs the index and desired-write witness.

recovery.detail: Opaque cursors bind store origin, pinned read cut, projection progress for every family read, desired-write generation, selection filters, page limit and last subject. Continuations must preserve filters and limit and validate the same current cut, projection progress and desired-write generation; a change returns typed desired-cursor-expired, including backlog projection advances without new claims and repair-driven selected-row rewrites at unchanged claim cut and graph health. There is no historical snapshot, pagination cache, silent restart or retry. The CLI follows cursors with unchanged filters and limit 1,000, prints one final array only on complete success, and fails without partial stdout on cursor invalidation. Older daemons lack the collection route; existing per-subject reads remain available.
